log.text: Stealth Rock up on P2's side
Toxic Spikes up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Garchomp leads with Focus Sash guaranteeing Stealth Rock setup. Gengar stays un-Mega'd for 178-Speed revenge-killing and Shadow Ball crushes Floette. Toxapex adds Toxic Spikes hazard pressure and Regenerator pivoting. Meowscarada gives Protean coverage, fastest speed (192) for cleaning, and U-turn to scout the opponent's unresolved 4th slot.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Manectric-Mega + Floette-Eternal deadly in rain; Sneasler Jolly/Life Orb/PoisonTouch runs Close Combat. Avoid Pelipper lead to deny rain. Prioritize dual-hazard setup (Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes). Shadow Tag on Mega Gengar insufficient follow-through last game—keep Gengar un-Mega'd for speed. Revenge-kill speed tier critical: Gengar 178, Meowscarada 192. Must scout slot 4 (Talonflame/Archaludon/Palafin) via U-turn pivot. Poison/Steel coverage essential vs Floette.

decisions.rationale: Repeat the successful Mega Manectric + Sneasler pressure lead into Pelipper/Mega Gengar, with Floette reserved for Garchomp/Clefable and Archaludon providing a sturdy special attacker plus Shuca-supported Ground insurance.
decisions.notebook: G1 opponent brought Pelipper + Gengar lead, Garchomp + Clefable back. Clefable used Light Screen when it entered. Mega Manectric + Sneasler strongly pressures the rain lead, especially Pelipper and Mega Gengar. Floette is a planned backline answer to Garchomp/Clefable and can threaten through Light Screen with Light of Ruin.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake would 2x our own Gengar (Ground vs Poison), so Garchomp sets Stealth Rock for dual-hazard pressure instead. Gengar fires neutral Shadow Ball STAB at Manectric—no reason to Mega and lose speed. Gengar acts first (178 Spe) to threaten before Garchomp rocks.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Manectric-Mega + Floette-Eternal deadly in rain; Sneasler Jolly/Life Orb/PoisonTouch runs Close Combat. Avoid Pelipper lead to deny rain. Dual-hazard setup: Stealth Rock now, Toxic Spikes via Toxapex later. Keep Gengar un-Mega'd for speed tier (178). Revenge-kill speed matters: Gengar 178, Meowscarada 192. Scout hidden slot 4 via U-turn pivot. Poison/Steel coverage essential vs Floette. Earthquake is unsafe due to Ground vs Poison 2x on own Gengar.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve for Intimidate and likely maximum Speed, Fake Out Garchomp to deny its immediate Earthquake, and Thunderbolt Mega Gengar for the strongest reliable direct pressure. This preserves Sneasler while forcing Gengar to absorb substantial damage or respond defensively.
decisions.notebook: G1 opponent brought Pelipper, Gengar, Garchomp, and Clefable; Clefable used Light Screen on entry. Opponent’s revealed sets: Gengar has Shadow Ball/Sludge Wave/Focus Blast/Thunderbolt with Gengarite; Garchomp has Focus Sash and Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Possible unrevealed G2 reserves are Pelipper, Clefable, Toxapex, or Meowscarada. Mega Manectric plus Sneasler provides strong pressure into Pelipper/Gengar; Floette is the intended Garchomp/Clefable answer and can pressure through Light Screen with Light of Ruin.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp sets Stealth Rock for long-term residual chip on both foes while it's weakened by poison. Gengar fires Shadow Ball at Manectric-Mega (32% HP) without Mega Evolving to preserve its speed tier and try to eliminate the faster revenge-kill threat.

Manectric-Mega weakened to 32%—try to eliminate this turn.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is poisoned at 56% with -1 Atk—passing preserves it. Switch Gengar to Meowscarada (Speed 192) to threaten the weakened 32% Manectric-Mega and scout the hidden slot via U-turn pivot.

Revenge-kill speed tier: Meowscarada 192 > Gengar 178. Scout hidden slot 4 via U-turn pivot next turn.

decisions.rationale: Overheat is a guaranteed KO on the revealed 24% Mega Gengar if it connects. Sneasler Protect denies Garchomp’s Earthquake while preserving it for the endgame; Manectric is otherwise guaranteed to fall to Earthquake from its current range.

Gengar: Gengarite, Shadow Ball/Sludge Wave/Focus Blast/Thunderbolt; Cursed Body can Disable a contacted/targeting move (Thunderbolt was disabled in G2). Garchomp: Focus Sash, Rough Skin, Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. G2 reserves remain among Pelipper, Clefable, Toxapex, Meowscarada. Mega Manectric + Sneasler pressures Pelipper/Gengar; Floette is the primary Garchomp/Clefable answer and can pressure through Light Screen with Light of Ruin.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Manectric-Mega (32% HP, -2 SpA) to force a KO or heavy damage. Garchomp's Stone Edge is super-effective and Meowscarada's U-turn pressures Manectric while pivoting Toxapex in safely. Toxapex walls Sneasler's Close Combat, sets Toxic Spikes, and scouts the hidden slot.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Preserve both damaged attackers from Garchomp’s Earthquake. Floette blanks Dragon Claw and threatens Garchomp, while Shuca Archaludon safely absorbs Ground pressure and gives a strong follow-up into Meowscarada or Garchomp.
decisions.notebook: Opponent G2 final reserve is one of Pelipper, Clefable, or Toxapex; Meowscarada is Life Orb Protean with Flower Trick/Sucker Punch/Brick Break/U-turn. Garchomp is Focus Sash Rough Skin with Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Preserve Mega Manectric when possible for Pelipper; Floette is the main Garchomp and Clefable answer, and Archaludon’s Shuca Berry is valuable for Ground matchups.

decisions.rationale: Preserve Mega Manectric for the likely Pelipper endgame. Sneasler is the safer immediate replacement and maintains offensive pressure into Garchomp while Archaludon remains available to punish Toxapex.
decisions.notebook: Opponent G2: Meowscarada is Life Orb Protean with Flower Trick/Sucker Punch/Brick Break/U-turn. Garchomp is Focus Sash Rough Skin, Jolly, with Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Toxapex is Bold Leftovers Regenerator with Recover/Baneful Bunker/Liquidation/Toxic Spikes. Preserve Mega Manectric when feasible for a potential Pelipper endgame; Floette is the primary Garchomp/Clefable answer, while Archaludon’s Shuca Berry is important versus Ground pressure.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp at 43% HP poisoned with -1 Atk is too frail to trade; switch to Meowscarada (192 Spe) to outspeed and threaten U-turn pivots while dodging Archaludon's super-effective Draco Meteor. Toxapex sets Toxic Spikes to complete the dual-hazard plan (Stealth Rock already up), pressuring future switches.

Fake Out guarantees Garchomp cannot use Earthquake this turn, and Archaludon’s Draco Meteor is a guaranteed KO from its shown HP range. This cleanly removes the immediate double Ground pressure while preserving Sneasler and Shuca Berry.

Preserve Mega Manectric when feasible for a potential Pelipper endgame; Floette is the primary Garchomp/Clefable answer, while Archaludon’s Shuca Berry is important versus Ground pressure.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake 2x hits both foes (Dragon/Ground super-effective on Sneasler and Archaludon) while Baneful Bunker protects Toxapex from the spread and poisons any contact move from Sneasler. This maximizes damage output while keeping Toxapex safe, crucial since Garchomp is already at 43% poisoned and may not get another turn.

Revenge-kill speed tier: Meowscarada 192 > Gengar 178. Scout hidden slot 4 via U-turn pivot. Manectric-Mega Intimidate weakens physical attackers. Need Poison/Steel coverage vs Floette if it returns. Archaludon at -2 SpA is neutered on special side; watch for Dragon Claw or coverage. Toxic Spikes on their side punish switches.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler is guaranteed faster than Garchomp, and Close Combat is a guaranteed KO from 43% before it can Earthquake. Archaludon then gets productive super-effective Thunderbolt chip on Toxapex; Baneful Bunker does not punish Thunderbolt.

Garchomp is Focus Sash Rough Skin, Jolly, with Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Toxapex is Bold Leftovers Regenerator with Recover/Baneful Bunker/Liquidation/Toxic Spikes. Preserve Mega Manectric when feasible for a potential Pelipper endgame; Floette is the primary Garchomp/Clefable answer, while Archaludon’s Shuca Berry is important versus Ground pressure. Garchomp is always slower than Jolly Sneasler but faster than Archaludon; its Sash has been broken this game. Toxapex cannot punish non-contact special attacks through Baneful Bunker.

selection: Baneful Bunker [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Toxapex at full HP should Baneful Bunker: it blocks Thunderbolt this turn, and any contact move from Sneasler (Close Combat/Gunk Shot) triggers poison on the foe. Archaludon's Thunderbolt is weakened by its -2 SpA. Recover is wasted at 100%. Liquidation is 0.5× to both foes. Garchomp is fainted so must pass.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Manectric-Mega + Sneasler + Archaludon. Sneasler Jolly/Life Orb/PoisonTouch, at -1/-1 defenses. Archaludon Modest/ShucaBerry, SpA at -2. Toxic Spikes and Stealth Rock on opponent side. Revenge-kill speed tier: Meowscarada 192 > Gengar 178. Need Poison/Steel coverage vs Floette-Eternal if it returns. Archaludon's low Speed makes it a potential TR target. All three of my other Pokémon are fainted—Toxapex is the last mon, prioritize survival and stalling. Save game 3 if this becomes unwinnable.

decisions.rationale: Double-targeting maximizes immediate pressure on Toxapex; Gunk Shot is Sneasler’s strongest available hit despite resistance, while Archaludon’s Thunderbolt is super-effective. Protecting Sneasler gives Toxapex too much room to Recover after only one weakened Thunderbolt.

Baneful Bunker is the only move that keeps Toxapex alive against Manectric-Mega's OHKO Thunderbolt. It blocks all incoming moves at +4 priority and can poison Sneasler on contact, creating the only path to chip damage and potential attrition. Any attacking move drops protection and lets Thunderbolt OHKO, so stalling with protection maximizes the slim chance of winning.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Manectric-Mega (Intimidate/Timid), Sneasler (PoisonTouch/Jolly/LifeOrb), Archaludon (Stamina/Modest/ShucaBerry). Opponent has Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes on their side. Sneasler at -1/-1 defenses, Archaludon at -2 SpA (resets next game). Floette-Eternal fainted. Opponent has 2 unknown benched Pokémon. Revenge-kill speed tier: Meowscarada 192 > Gengar 178. For game 3: need Poison/Steel coverage for Floette-Eternal if it returns; Archaludon's low Speed makes it a TR target; watch for Manectric-Mega Intimidate on lead.

decisions.rationale: Switching Mega Manectric in creates a guaranteed two-Thunderbolt KO if Toxapex does anything except Baneful Bunker; passive Sneasler is otherwise immediately vulnerable to Liquidation. This forces its only meaningful defensive line while retaining Archaludon pressure.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s remaining G2 Pokémon is Bold Leftovers Regenerator Toxapex with Recover, Baneful Bunker, Liquidation, and Toxic Spikes. Baneful Bunker blocks both attackers but cannot safely be relied on consecutively. Mega Manectric plus Archaludon Thunderbolt pressure is the clearest route through Toxapex; avoid contact into Bunker unless necessary. Preserve Mega Manectric for Pelipper in future games when feasible. Garchomp is Jolly Focus Sash Rough Skin; Meowscarada is Jolly Life Orb Protean; Gengar is Timid Gengarite.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is fainted with no viable switch-ins, so Pass is forced. Toxapex uses Recover to heal to full HP, maximizing its chance of surviving the incoming triple attack (Manectric-Mega Thunderbolt 2x, Archaludon Thunderbolt 2x at -2 SpA, Sneasler Gunk Shot). Manectric-Mega at 8% HP with poison will likely faint next turn, dramatically improving the position.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Manectric-Mega (Intimidate/Timid), Sneasler (PoisonTouch/Jolly/LifeOrb), Archaludon (Stamina/Modest/ShucaBerry). Archaludon SpA at -2 resets next game. Opponent hazards: Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes on their side (both set by me). Revenge-kill tier: Meowscarada 192 > Gengar 178. For game 3: need Poison/Steel coverage for Floette-Eternal if it returns; Archaludon low Speed makes it a TR target; watch Manectric-Mega Intimidate on lead.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt from Mega Manectric is a guaranteed KO on Toxapex from its shown range if Baneful Bunker fails; Archaludon’s Thunderbolt adds damage if needed. A consecutive successful Bunker is unreliable, and Manectric will otherwise succumb to poison.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 due to fundamental team-building missteps against the opponent's core. Mega Gengar was a poor lead and Mega pick — Manectric-Mega's Intimidate neutered it and Garchomp, while Overheat OHKOd Gengar outright. Meowscarada, the only revenge killer (192 Spe), was eliminated by Sneasler Fake Out + Archaludon Draco Meteor before it could clean up. Garchomp was passivated by Intimidate + poison + Stealth Rock chip and fell to Sneasler Close Combat. Toxapex was the only Pokémon that stayed alive but couldn't break through; Baneful Bunker was repeatedly shut down by Protect, and it lacked the offensive pressure to threaten the opponent's bulky core. Pelipper and Clefable — both unpicked — could have provided rain support, Fairy coverage for Floette-Eternal, and utility (Follow Me, Thunder Wave). The opponent shifted their team between games (adding Floette-Eternal, Archaludon) and I failed to adapt my six or strategy accordingly. The game was unwinnable once Gengar and Meowscarada fell because Toxapex alone had no path to break three defensive/offensive threats.
reflections.adjustment: Drop Mega Gengar — it loses to Manectric-Mega Intimidate and provides no defensive utility. Bring Clefable back for Follow Me/Encore utility, Moonblast on Floette-Eternal, and Thunder Wave on Manectric and Archaludon. Bring Pelipper back for rain, which dampens Manectric's Fire coverage and powers up Liquidation on Toxapex. Consider Skarmory over one slot for Spikes + Whirlwind pressure and Intimidate/Steelix physical bulk against Sneasler Close Combat. Game plan: lead with a safe pivot (Clefable/Toxapex), set up rain with Pelipper, use Baneful Bunker Toxapex to stall Manectric while building Toxic Spikes damage, and look to revenge-kill with priority or a fast U-turn pivot rather than committing Meowscarada into unfavorable matchups. Never U-turn into Floette-Eternal again — it resists and the crit was not enough. Prioritize removing Archaludon (ShucaBerry makes it hard to OHKO) with repeated Thunderbolts under rain or strong neutral hits before it can set up a Draco Meteor.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core pattern: Manectric-Mega (Intimidate/Timid) always mega-turn 1 to cripple physical attackers; Sneasler (PoisonTouch/LifeOrb/Jolly) lead with Fake Out, pressures physical walls with Close Combat + Gunk Shot; Archaludon (Stamina/Modest/ShucaBerry) is primary special breaker with Thunderbolt spam, Draco Meteor nuke, and Flash Cannon coverage — ShucaBerry lets it survive Water/Ground hits; Floette-Eternal (FlowerVeil/Timid) is a bulky Fairy special wall with Moonblast and nuke-potential Light of Ruin, resists U-turn. Opponent uses Protect extensively for scouting and stalling. Opponent sets Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes through team support. Key takeaway: Intimidate + Manectric-Mega hard-counters any physical sweeper I lead with; revenge-kill speed tier matters (Meowscarada 192 > Gengar 178 but both fell before cleaning). Archaludon SpA drop from Draco Meteor resets each game — treat it as full-power next time. Toxapex can survive but needs offensive partners; Baneful Bunker is useless if opponent Protect-stalls. Clefable and Pelipper are must-brings for next series against this opponent. Rain neutralizes Manectric's Overheat and powers Toxapex Liquidation. Priority or fast pivots needed to handle Sneasler after Fake Out.

reflections.summary: You won game 2 and the series 2-0 because Mega Manectric, Sneasler, and Archaludon matched the opponent’s Gengar/Garchomp/Meowscarada/Toxapex core well: Fake Out plus Intimidate disrupted the lead, Manectric removed Gengar and later pressured Toxapex, and Archaludon/Sneasler converted the midgame into a clean endgame. The four brought were broadly correct, and Mega Evolving Manectric rather than Floette was the right matchup call. Floette was the weak point of the selection/pivot plan, being lost after a critical U-turn and Stone Edge, but the remaining three covered the matchup. No evidence from game 1 is supplied, so the specific between-game adjustment cannot be isolated; game 2’s selection and execution clearly helped rather than backfired. Series prep correctly registered strong answers to this revealed core, especially Manectric, Sneasler, and Archaludon. There is insufficient evidence to claim any omitted Pokémon or unknown omitted sets would have been better.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain Mega Manectric + Sneasler + Archaludon as a primary anti-Gengar/Garchomp/Toxapex package. Prioritize preserving Manectric for Gengar, Toxapex, and potentially Pelipper; use Sneasler’s Fake Out to deny Garchomp or Meowscarada tempo, then let Archaludon supply sustained Electric pressure. Be more cautious about bringing or pivoting Floette into the Garchomp/Meowscarada pairing, since it can be exposed to U-turn chip and Stone Edge. Against Toxapex, avoid contact moves into Baneful Bunker when possible and pressure it with both Electric attackers, exploiting the unreliability of repeated Bunker.
reflections.notebook: Opponent revealed Timid Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball, Sludge Wave, Focus Blast, Thunderbolt, and Cursed Body; Jolly Focus Sash Rough Skin Garchomp with Earthquake, Stone Edge, Dragon Claw, Stealth Rock; Jolly Life Orb Protean Meowscarada with Flower Trick, Sucker Punch, Brick Break, U-turn; and Bold Leftovers Regenerator Toxapex with Recover, Baneful Bunker, Liquidation, Toxic Spikes. Their G2 composition favored Gengar/Garchomp/Meowscarada/Toxapex over Pelipper/Clefable. Toxapex uses Baneful Bunker as a major stalling tool, but consecutive use is not dependable; dual Electric pressure is the clearest answer. Garchomp’s Sash and Stealth Rock make early chip valuable. Mega Manectric’s Intimidate and Electric pressure, Sneasler’s Fake Out, and Archaludon’s attacks were the strongest confirmed prep elements; Floette was less secure into the revealed physical pressure.
